interpretation: Instruction (from ep.observe()): 'pick up the red cube and lift it.' The scene held a single object, obj1, perceived as 'red · 4x4x3 cm' (the depth-only perception missed the bottom few mm). Measured from its top-face points it is a ~3.9-4.0 cm red cube, top face centred at (0.537, -0.022), top at z=-0.072, resting on the table at z=-0.111 (robot-root frame), axis-aligned within ~2 deg. Goal state: the red cube grasped in the gripper and raised clearly off the table, still held when the episode ends. Nothing was ambiguous: there is only one object, and it is red and cubic. 'Lift' gives no height, so I chose a clear lift of ~20 cm.
plan: Robot: robosuite Panda ('capx_robosuite_panda'), 7 joints, one scene camera (robot0_robotview, at x=1.0, z=0.4, looking back at the robot), no wrist camera. Parallel-jaw gripper: closing axis x, approach axis z, 8 cm stroke, max_width 0.079, closed_empty 0.985, held_below 0.95. Plan: top-down grasp with the fingers closing along world y (the cube's faces). (1) Open the gripper while moving to a pre-grasp 10 cm above the cube's top. (2) Descend straight down to TCP z=-0.088, about the cube's mid-height (centre -0.092) and 1.6 cm below its top. This keeps the conservative finger spheres (up to 2.2 cm past the TCP) at the table and the real fingertips about 1 cm above it. (3) Close and read gripper_measured. (4) Lift 6 cm to confirm the grip, then continue to +20 cm. (5) Check from the RGB image and depth, then finish while holding. Two changes along the way: I first tried rh.top_down yaw -90, but that needed a half-turn of the wrist (q7 from -2.39 to +0.15); the preview was refused (joint-7 limit, unreachable, too fast), so I used yaw +90, the same physical closing axis with q7 about -2.42. The gripper opened only partly during the first move (reading 0.471), so I added an explicit 1 s open before descending.

steps.what: Read the robot description, instruction, budget; listed objects; showed robot0_robotview RGB, annotated ids and 3D views
steps.why: Identify the robot, camera, gripper and target object before planning
steps.result: Panda, 1 scene camera, 1500 steps at control_dt 0.05 (75 s of motion). One object, obj1, the red cube. Gripper started commanded closed, reading 0.79.

steps.what: Measured the table (ep.pick on 6 table pixels) and the cube's top-face points (object_points); inspected the gripper's collision spheres in the TCP frame
steps.why: Get an exact grasp position and a grasp height that keeps the fingertips off the table
steps.result: Table z=-0.1113. Cube top face centre (0.5372, -0.0217) at z=-0.0722, size about 3.99 x 3.90 cm. Finger spheres reach at most 2.2 cm past the TCP along the approach axis.

steps.what: IK and preview of the pre-grasp at yaw -90, then at yaw +90
steps.why: Choose the wrist orientation for closing along world y
steps.result: Yaw -90 refused (wrist half-turn: joint-7 limit, unreachable, too fast). Yaw +90 ok: 2.8 s, no issues, arm collision-free in check_batch.

steps.what: Executed the move to the pre-grasp (0.537, -0.022, 0.028) with gripper 0
steps.why: Get above the cube with the gripper opening
steps.result: Done in 56 steps (step 56), within about 1 mm of the target. The gripper had only opened to 0.471 (gap 4.2 cm), too narrow for a 4 cm cube.

steps.why: Open fully before descending around the cube

steps.what: Previewed the descent to TCP z=-0.088 and checked it with check_batch; overlaid the grasp pose on the camera image and rendered a ghost at the end pose
steps.why: Verify the fingers straddle the cube and stay clear of it
steps.result: Preview ok. check_batch flagged finger-sphere contacts with obj1 (up to 2.2 cm deep). Those spheres span the whole space between the fingers; the real pads sit at +/-3.9 cm against the cube's +/-2.1 cm half-width, and the camera overlay and the ghost both showed the fingers on either side of the cube. I judged the contacts to be from the sphere model and executed.

steps.why: Put the finger pads at the cube's sides
steps.result: Done in 46 steps (step 122), TCP error 0 mm. The camera crop showed open fingers on both sides of the cube, and the cube was undisturbed (its aabb unchanged).

Reading 0.477, gap 4.19 cm, which matches the cube's width and is well below held_below 0.95, so it is held (step 152). The image showed the pads clamped on both sides. The cube dropped out of objects(), merged with the robot; held=None.

steps.why: Confirm the grip holds before the full lift
steps.result: Done in 42 steps (step 194). The cube rose with the gripper, the table where it stood was empty, and the reading stayed 0.477.

steps.what: Lifted to 20 cm above the grasp height (TCP z=0.112, 2.5 s)
steps.why: Lift the cube clearly off the table
steps.result: Done in 56 steps (step 250). The reading stayed 0.477, and the RGB image shows the cube between the pads high above the table.

steps.what: Final verification: depth (ep.pick) at the red pixels, an RGB crop, and 3D views of the cloud
steps.why: The robot has only one camera, so I used its RGB plus its depth and 3D view as independent checks of each part of the instruction
steps.result: The cube's visible faces are at z=0.094..0.129, i.e. 20.5-24 cm above the table (z=-0.111). The cloud shows the table empty where the cube was. finish_episode was called at step 250 of 1500.

key_images.caption: Start: the red cube obj1 alone on the table, id overlaid on robot0_robotview
Planned path to the pre-grasp 10 cm above the cube (yaw +90, gripper opening)
Ghost robot at the grasp pose: fingers straddle the cube
At grasp height: open fingers on both sides of the cube
After closing: pads clamped on the cube (reading 0.477, gap 4.19 cm)
After the first 6 cm lift: cube rising with the gripper
Final: cube held about 20 cm above the table; table empty
Final close-up: cube between the finger pads
Final 3D cloud view: nothing left on the table, gripper raised

lessons: 1) Choose the top-down yaw by IK against the current q, not by the finger_yaw value alone. finger_yaw read -89 deg at the start, but the matching rh.top_down yaw was +90; yaw -90 needed a wrist half-turn that the preview refused. Both close along world y. 2) A gripper command carried on a motion waypoint may not finish during the motion: the gripper had opened only to 0.471 after the 2.8 s move. Read gripper_measured and give an explicit ep.gripper(0) before descending around an object close to half the stroke. 3) This Panda's finger collision spheres fill the space between the fingers, so check_batch flags 'contacts' with any object between open fingers. Judge clearance from the measured gap, the object's width and the camera image. 4) Perception folds a grasped object into the robot (it leaves objects(), held=None), so verify the lift by depth at the object's colour pixels and by the gripper reading staying below held_below. 5) Measuring the object from its top-face points gives a more accurate grasp centre than the perceived centroid, which the visible front face biased by about 8 mm in +x here.
